p01.why: A reference member of a prvalue gives an lvalue, so int& binds to it; there is no main.

p02.why: A static data member gives an lvalue even through a class prvalue, so its address can be taken.

p03.why: s.m and p->m are lvalues, so decltype((...)) is int& and & is valid.

p04.why: A cast to an rvalue reference to a function type gives an lvalue, so its address can be taken.

p05.why: The name of an rvalue reference variable is an lvalue, so decltype((r)) is int&.

p06.why: The throwing copy into the parameter and the throwing destructor of the parameter both happen in the caller, so both handlers run and caught is 21.

p07.why: Both temporaries live to the end of the full expression, so use sees n == 0, and they end in reverse creation order before 9 is logged.

p08.why: The references extend the two temporaries to the end of the block, so no destructor runs inside and both run at its end.

p09.why: r binds to the temporary and m to a member of another temporary, and both lifetimes are extended.

p10.why: val() is an int prvalue, which cannot be assigned to.

p11.why: The converting constructor throws while the caller initializes the parameter, so the caller catches 3 despite noexcept.

p12.why: The discarded Probe temporary lives to the end of the full expression, so count() sees 1, and it is gone afterwards.

p13.why: Members initialize in declaration order and each member initializer is a full expression, so the trace is 1, 5, 2, 5.

p14.why: a << 1 is a prvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p15.why: A call that returns int&& is an xvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p16.why: this is a prvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p17.why: In the operand of decltype a call makes no temporary, so the deleted destructor is not needed.

p18.why: Constant evaluation makes the temporaries for the member call and member access, and f() is 7.

p19.why: The temporary lives during take and ends with the assignment's full expression.

p20.why: The discarded class prvalue becomes a temporary that ends at the end of its statement, before 9 is logged; no copy is made.

p21.why: An int lvalue and an int prvalue give an int prvalue, which cannot be assigned to.

p22.why: All initializers of one aggregate are one full expression, so both temporaries end after both reads: 1, 2, 9, 9.

p23.why: make() is an int prvalue, which cannot be assigned to.

p24.why: The caller destroys s a second time; Clang and GCC reject this in constant evaluation, and EDG accepts parameter-destroyed-by-callee-constant.cpp.

p25.why: Subscripting the array prvalue makes a temporary, and element 1 is 2.

p26.why: The temporary of the expression statement ends at the end of that statement.

p27.why: Each prvalue initializes its object directly, so only two S objects are made.

p28.why: val() is a prvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p29.why: A class prvalue can be assigned to, because the assignment is a member function call.

p30.why: The init capture belongs to the enclosing full expression, so Note{3} ends after mark(4): trace 43.

p31.why: An enumerator is a prvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p32.why: The temporary for the member call ends at the end of the declaration, before mark(3).

p33.why: Whether the parameter shares the caller's address is unspecified, and the program accepts both.

p34.why: Both temporaries last to the end of the full expression and end in reverse order, 2 then 1.

p35.why: A subscript of an array xvalue or array prvalue is an xvalue, so decltype gives int&&; EDG gives an lvalue for the first (Q-0034).

p36.why: The two parameter objects end in some order, and the program accepts both.

p37.why: Each expression is an xvalue, so decltype((...)) is int&&.

p38.why: A non-class prvalue has no cv-qualifiers, so the call has type int.

p39.why: Each expression is a prvalue, so decltype((...)) gives the plain type.

p40.why: p is an lvalue, so int&& cannot bind to it.

p41.why: this, an enumerator, a cast to non-reference, and x,0 are prvalues; a cast to int& and 0,x are lvalues.

p42.why: Each for clause is its own full expression, so no Probe lives during the body.

p43.why: .* on a class prvalue makes a temporary that ends with the declaration, before mark(2).

p44.why: The array prvalue becomes a temporary that lives through the call.

p45.why: With a default argument per element, each element's temporaries end before the next element: 1, 9, 1, 9.

p46.why: The discarded class prvalue makes a temporary, so its destructor must be usable, and it is deleted.

p47.why: .* applied to an xvalue for a data member gives an xvalue.

p48.why: Three parameter objects end in some order, and the program accepts every order.

p49.why: The default argument's temporary lives to the end of the full expression with the call: 1, 9, 2.

p50.why: Prvalues initialize a and b directly, so the deleted copy and move constructors are never needed.

p51.why: A condition is a full expression, so T ends before the body runs: 9, 1.

p52.why: A cast to int&& gives an xvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p53.why: a + b is a prvalue, and its address cannot be taken.

p54.why: Each expression is an lvalue, a string literal included.

p55.why: The array prvalue converts to a pointer through a temporary that lives through the call.

p56.why: The parameter ends either at the return or at the end of the caller's full expression, and the program accepts both.

p57.why: The temporary lives until the end of the declaration, after read: 1, 9, 2.

p58.why: Each declarator's initializer is its own full expression: 1, 9, 2, 9.

p59.why: A member access that names a non-static member function can only be called.

p60.why: The address comparison is unspecified, and the program accepts both results.

p61.why: A const int lvalue and a volatile int lvalue give a prvalue, whose address cannot be taken.
